parishes of glendermott & strathfoyle sunday 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time the commandment of love is the greatest of the commandments, the mother of all the virtues, and the pulsating heart of the christian message. we are created in the image of a god who is love; so, we cannot live without love in today’s gospel reading from matthew, one of the pharisees, a lawyer, asks jesus to identify ‘the greatest commandment of the law’(mt 22:36). in response, jesus quotes the great ‘shema’ prayer recited daily by all devout jews (cf. deut 6:4-5). this prayer exhorts us to love god with our whole heart, mind and soul. jesus immediately adds a second commandment, familiar to his audience namely, ‘love your neighbour as yourself’ (mt 22:39). sadly, the word ‘love’ is so overused in our world today that it has lost much of its meaning. we speak of love of country, love of sport, love of food, love between friends, love of parents, romantic love, etc as pope leo teaches, ‘true love is not merely a fleeting, briefly inflamed emotion. it is more. it is a deep commitment to the other, a decision, a journey and a covenant for life all genuine love is manifested in action; it is practical and outgoing. in the words of st augustine: ‘it has the hands to help others. it has the feet to hasten to the poor and needy. it has the eyes to see misery and want. it has the ears to hear the sighs and sorrows of people.’ such love is demanding. it summons us to leave our comfort zones, to give our time, our energy, our talents, and, indeed, our very selves to others feast of all saints mass arrangements for the feast of all saints- saturday 31st october 6:00pm church of immaculate conception 6:00pm st. oliver plunkett 6:30pm st. columb’s church (note change of time) waterside strathfoyle amalgamated)

diocesan appointments - this weekend is fr lagan’s last weekend in our parish as our priest, i take the opportunity to thank him sincerely for his work both in the parish and the hospitals over the past four years. his endearing personality enabled him to get to know many people in a short period of time. his good humour and generosity of time have brought many blessings to many people and our parish community. as he begins a new phase of his life as parish priest in the sperrin parishes of gortin and greencastle, i on behalf of the parish, wish him every blessing. it will be a very big change for him so let’s keep him and all the priests involved in the latest diocesan appointments in our prayers. words of thanks from fr lagan on 18th august 2022, bishop donal mckeown appointed me to the parishes of glendermott and strathfoyle. on that occasion, even though it was a change, i very much knew that i was coming home. i was sent to a parish that i had previously served and for a short while after my ordination in 2012 began ministering as a priest. it is a place that i love very much and this last four years have been both a time of immense blessing. on 9th october, bishop router appointed me to the parishes of greencastle and gortin in co tyrone. whilst i am deeply honoured for his trust in me, i leave here with the best preparation i could ask for in taking up this new challenge. i want to thank all the staff of our parish, those who work to support the running of glendermott and strathfoyle, but especially to fr joshi for his kindness, guidance, support and friendship and to fr michael canny for his ever willing example, paternal guidance and endless patience not only during my time here but throughout my priestly ministry and also to each of you, for your prayers, your faith filled example and for the love and kindness that you have shown me, i will forever treasure. please keep me in your prayers and be assured of my prayers for you, your loved ones and families in the months and years ahead. thank you. baptisms – we welcome into god’s family: noah doherty birch hill, cailean john christopher tracey deramore drive. anniversaries – for those
